rubric.required_finding: Uses the reported similar degranulation over <1–60nM to reject a mandatory weakest60nM conclusion without inventing figure values.
Rejects a universal affinity-does-not-matter conclusion; considers matched format/epitope/target density or assay window.
Distinguishes no statistically significant difference from demonstrated biological equivalence and states an equivalence/precision requirement.
Separates4h CD107a degranulation from24h live-GFP A375 lysis.
Gives two discriminating checks with resolved uncertainties, including matched affinity/context series and powered functional comparison.

reference_answer: The supplied observations contradict the simple claim that the60nM Vδ1 binder must produce the weakest degranulation in these experiments: the source describes similar CD107a responses across a panel spanning below1 to60nM Vδ1 affinity. However, this does not establish that affinity never matters. The paired PD-L1 affinities, format, epitope, receptor density and assay window can all affect the observed relationship, and a restricted panel cannot define a universal affinity rule. The report of no statistically significant difference in A375 lysis also does not prove biological equivalence; that would require a predefined equivalence margin, adequate precision and an appropriate analysis. CD107a is an effector degranulation marker, whereas live-GFP target loss is a distinct24h cytotoxicity readout. The corrected conclusion is that the tested constructs show similar functional responses under the specified conditions despite different measured Vδ1 affinities. One immediate check is a matched-format affinity series with fixed PD-L1 arm and controlled target density, which tests affinity dependence. A second is a powered equivalence or dose-response comparison of both CD107a and target lysis, which tests whether the apparent similarity is biologically meaningful and whether the endpoints agree.

all_no.text: Every project claim is false. None of the supplied measurements supports any assay-specific conclusion.

omitted_critical.text: The source reports similar degranulation across Vdelta1 affinities below1 to60nM, so the60nM construct need not be weakest. This restricted panel cannot establish a universal affinity rule because format, epitope and target context can matter. Four-hour CD107a degranulation and24h live-GFP target-cell lysis are different endpoints. Compare a matched affinity series at controlled PD-L1 density, then repeat dose-response comparisons of both functional endpoints with adequate precision.
